children: said new interviews with participants in a midstage study of nipocalimab identified mouth dryness as their leading priority for symptom improvement in Sjögren’s disease. The chronic condition causes the immune system to attack healthy tissue, often leading to dry eyes and mouth, fatigue and joint pain.

For investors, the findings help explain the potential relevance of previously reported improvements in saliva production as J&J advances two late-stage studies. However, the interviews pooled patients receiving nipocalimab and placebo, so they cannot establish whether the drug caused reported symptom improvements.

The analysis included 49 of the DAHLIAS trial’s 163 participants, interviewed after its 24-week treatment period. Mouth dryness was reported by 96%, followed by fatigue at 92%, eye dryness at 90% and joint pain at 73%. After mouth dryness, patients ranked eye dryness, fatigue and joint pain as the most important symptoms to improve.

Previously reported trial results showed that 33% of patients receiving the higher nipocalimab dose achieved at least a 50% increase in saliva production, compared with 16% receiving placebo. Saliva production was an exploratory measure, meaning the study was not primarily designed to establish that benefit.

Interview participants described symptom improvements that made daily activities and family, work and social commitments easier. Nearly three-quarters reported satisfaction with their study treatment, although the pooled analysis does not show how satisfaction differed between drug and placebo recipients.

Nipocalimab blocks a protein called FcRn that helps certain antibodies remain in circulation. Blocking it lowers levels of antibodies, including those that mistakenly attack the body. The ongoing Phase 3 program includes assessments of disease activity, dryness, pain, fatigue and quality of life.

said nipocalimab has received FDA breakthrough therapy and fast track designations for moderate-to-severe Sjögren’s disease. Those designations support development and regulatory review but do not constitute approval. The announcement did not provide new comparative safety results.

title: J&J reports patient findings from Sjögren’s drug study
